title: Session fission — feature scribble
body:
Context:

Quick brain dump for a lightweight feature concept I sketched during the developer sync. Working name = 'session fission' — idea is to reduce per-request context bloat and enable fine-grained personalization without duplicating sensitive material across model calls. This is intentionally rough. Notes to self + rough PRD outline.

Problem we keep hitting:
- Large sessions with mixed content (user prefs, transient instructions, long conversation history) lead to high token cost and slow inference.
- Teams want per-user personalization (preferences, persona tweaks) but can't safely or cheaply carry private data into every model call.
- Current prefix-caching approaches are monolithic: either cache full prefix (costly) or evict too aggressively (lossy).

Hypothesis:
- If we logically split session state into small, addressable sub-blocks (fissioned shards) and let the runtime assemble only the needed shards per request, we can reduce tokens and leakage surface while supporting persistent personalization.

Goals (success criteria):
- Reduce average prompt tokens per request for personalized sessions by >= 30% in targeted flows.
- Make personal data residency explicit: personal shards can be pinned to Private/Dedicated while general shards stay on Hosted.
- Enable quick developer ergonomics: SDK endpoint to register/update shards, and per-request hint to include shards by id.

Non-goals:
- This is not an auth or encryption design doc — rely on existing KMS + encryption transport.
- Not attempting to replace full session replay or stream-based conversational caches.

Core idea / primitive:
- Shard: small named chunk of context (1–800 tokens). Metadata: id, name, tags, scope (user/global/tenant), TTL, freshness score.
- Registry: lightweight metadata store mapping session -> list of shard ids (pinned or ephemeral). Could be in-memory with optional durable backing.
- Composer: runtime component that, given a request, picks shards to materialize into the model prompt based on hints + policies (cost budget, latency SLO, recency).

Developer surface (sketch):
- SDK: client.shards.create({ name, scope, content, ttl, tags }) -> shard_id
- SDK: client.shards.update(shard_id, { content, ttl })
- API: generate({ model, input, shards: ["shard_id", { id: "s2", priority: 0.8 }], shard_budget_tokens: 300 })
- Console: per-user shard viewer, retention controls, usage stats per shard id.

Policy examples (runtime heuristics):
- High-priority shards (user PINNED) always included until TTL expired.
- Budget-based selection: attempt to include highest-freshness shards until shard_budget_tokens consumed.
- Sensitivity lanes: shards marked sensitive may only be assembled on Dedicated/private runtimes. If request on Hosted, composer can substitute a sanitized variant or skip.

User stories (rough):
- As a developer, I want to store a user's display preferences as a shard so I can apply them to generation without sending the entire conversation history every time.
- As a product manager, I want to flag a shard as 'PII' so it is never routed to Hosted inference.
- As an operator, I want metrics per shard (inclusions, avg tokens contributed, miss rate) so we can tune TTLs and budgets.

Acceptance criteria (v0):
- SDK + server can create/update/delete shards for a session id.
- Composer respects per-request shard list and budget and returns assembled prompt for inspection.
- Basic console view shows shards and counts.
- E2E smoke: a simple chat app can reduce prompt tokens by at least 20% for a user with a preferences shard + 3 ephemeral context shards.

Metrics to track:
- avg_prompt_tokens_with_personalization vs baseline
- shard_inclusion_rate, shard_miss_rate
- avg_inference_latency_when_using_shards
- fraction_of_shards_marked_sensitive and routing outcomes

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0: internal experiment — SDK + in-memory registry + composer stub. Integrate into dev playground.
- Phase 1: public beta for select Hosted customers with console controls, limit to non-sensitive shards.
- Phase 2: Dedicated/private support for sensitive shards and routing policies.

Risks & open questions:
- Complexity surface: shard metadata management adds bookkeeping—how lightweight can we make it?
- Consistency tradeoffs: if shard content updates mid-request, need deterministic snapshot semantics. Always assemble on read snapshot.
- Observable billing: how to surface per-shard token cost cleanly?
- Privacy: does shardization create accidental inference channels? Need red-team review.

Implementation notes / ideas:
- Start with a simple in-memory per-runtime registry keyed by session id. Backfill to durable store when persistence is requested.
- Composer can be a lightweight scoring function: score = freshness * relevance_hint * (1 / token_count). Tuneable.
- Provide an automated 'shard-suggestion' tool that identifies repetitive small blocks in session history and suggests conversion to shards.

UI sketches (text):
- Shard list for user "u_123": [ "prefs-v1" (128t), "tone-guide" (40t), "last-order-summary" (220t) ] with quick toggles (pin, mark-sensitive, set-ttl).

Next steps (immediate):
- Prototype composer + SDK client shim in the dev playground (owner = me). 2-day spike to validate token reduction on a sample assistant use-case.
- Share spike results with Applied ML + Privacy for feasibility and risk signoff.

Notes to self (todo):
- Add examples of shard content shapes (json instruction, small vector embedding ref, short persona snippets).
- Draft console UX wireframe with cost-per-shard breakdown.
- Draft an explainer for customers: when to shard vs when to use full session.

Random thoughts (brainstorm):
- Could combine with KV-cache: shards that are mostly static become cacheable on GPU-side to avoid re-marshaling tokens.
- Offer a "shard diff" operation for efficient updates (patch content rather than replace).
- Consider a 'shard template' marketplace of common shards (e.g., polite-tone, legal-disclaimer) devs can adopt.

End of scribble. This is messy — will tidy after spike.
